speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; the mechanism of injury suggests a traumatic event. Given the swelling and pain in the ring finger, do you have any trouble extending your middle finger, and is there any numbness or tingling in that digit?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: That inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint of your right ring finger, combined with the history of a finger being caught and pulled, strongly suggests a rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon. Can you confirm if your middle finger also has a difficult time bending when you try to make a fist? REQUEST IMAGES: Right hand X-Ray and Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Flexor Digitorum Profundus (FDP) Rupture of the Right Ring Finger.

The history of the finger being caught and pulled, combined with the specific inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint while the rest of the finger can extend, is classic for this injury. The X-ray and ultrasound images requested earlier should confirm the tendon discontinuity and rule out associated fractures.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
